headline: Attackers using agentic AI to hunt exposed secrets; patched Zyxel GS1900 switches still exploitable; WordPress KEV due today

bullets.text: New, Microsoft: threat actors are using agentic AI tooling to find and abuse exposed secrets. Separately, Truffle Security launched a program targeting nearly 1.5 million live exposed secrets for revocation, and Chainalysis warned all users were hit in a breach involving 'agentic' techniques.
New, FBI and CISA: critical infrastructure operators are warned to harden refrigeration and cooling systems amid ongoing cyberattacks.

Still active, Zyxel GS1900, 4 outlets: Zyxel's fix for a zero-day used to hack nearly 1,000 switches did not block the in-the-wild exploit (CVE-2026-107441), which allows root command execution. SITCON remains 2 (SEVERE).

Due today, WordPress Core: CISA KEV lists CVE-2026-119977, a TOCTOU race condition exploited for RCE, with a federal due date of 2026-11-06. Apple CVE-2024-27834 (exploited for info-stealers) is due 2026-11-18.

Still active: OpenSSH emergency fix for a flaw letting long passwords bypass SSH auth on Alpine Linux (3 outlets); cPGuard autoupdate hijacked in the OpsShield supply-chain attack to deploy a backdoor (4 outlets).

Breaches: DigiCert exposed customer information and identity documents; DreamHost confirmed exposed FTP logins and webmail sessions; ransomware disrupted Queens Public Library. The last 7 days scored 0.63x the 90-day average.

actions: Scan repos, CI logs and public buckets for exposed secrets and rotate any found; assume automated discovery is running against you.
Patch WordPress Core for CVE-2026-119977 today (KEV due 2026-11-06).
Treat Zyxel GS1900 switches as exposed even after patching: restrict management access, check for compromise, watch for a new fix.
Apply the OpenSSH emergency fix on Alpine Linux hosts and restrict SSH password auth until patched.
cPGuard users: hunt for the backdoor delivered via autoupdate and rotate credentials on affected servers.
Operators of refrigeration and cooling systems: remove internet exposure of controllers and follow the FBI/CISA hardening guidance.
